headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Planning Additional Living Quarters
articleBody:
Creating an in-law suite or secondary living area is an exciting project, but it carries strict technical requirements that catch many homeowners off guard. Here are key pitfalls to watch for when planning secondary quarters:

1. Assuming finished spaces are automatically legal
Converting a garage, detached shed, or bonus room without building permits creates major safety hazards and disclosure headaches down the road. Local codes require verified ceiling heights, compliant light, and proper ventilation.

2. Overlooking emergency egress requirements
Any sleeping room must feature a compliant emergency escape window or door directly to the exterior with specific minimum opening dimensions.

3. Neglecting separate utility loads
Adding a full bathroom, kitchenette, and cooling to separate quarters puts significant demand on your electrical panel and plumbing lines. Failing to calculate utility capacity can cause tripped breakers or low water pressure.

4. Ignoring local zoning definitions
Different municipalities regulate guest suites and accessory dwelling units differently. Assuming a detached space can automatically have a full kitchen may violate local land-use rules.

5. Skipping soundproofing between shared walls
Failing to install insulation or resilient drywall channels between main living zones and guest quarters leads to noise complaints and privacy issues.
